fact_check_verdict: Publish as an allegation-and-settlement story. GM admitted no violation. Never '36 states', never 'scores', never an Alaska driver count, never a payout for drivers.

claims.spoken: General Motors will pay two hundred twenty million dollars.
requires: Say 'per the settlement'. GM admitted no violation of law.

claims.spoken: Thirty-six attorneys general signed on, and Alaska is one of them.
requires: Never say '36 states'. It is 35 states plus D.C.

claims.spoken: Alaska's share is two point five million dollars.
requires: Attribute to the Alaska Department of Law as reported by Alaska's News Source. Primary release unreachable.

claims.spoken: The attorneys general say G M enrolled millions of drivers in Smart Driver from twenty sixteen to twenty twenty-four.
requires: Attribute to the attorneys general. The complaint says 2015 launch.

claims.spoken: Smart Driver tracked hard braking, hard acceleration, and late-night driving.
requires: Alleged in the complaint.

claims.spoken: The complaint says G M also recorded precise location every three seconds.
requires: Alleged in the complaint.

claims.spoken: The complaint says G M sold that data to Verisk and to LexisNexis.
requires: Alleged. Neither news story names the brokers.

claims.spoken: Those companies built driver ratings and sold them to insurance companies.
requires: Alleged. Say 'driver ratings', not 'scores'.

claims.spoken: Some insurers used that information in part to set rates.
claims.on_screen: SOME INSURERS USED IT IN PART TO SET RATES
requires: Alleged. 'Some insurers', 'in part'.

claims.spoken: The complaint says G M made over twenty million dollars from the data sales.
requires: Alleged in the complaint.

claims.spoken: G M's apps told over three hundred seventy thousand people they weren't enrolled, while it collected their data.
requires: Alleged. Complaint blames a technical glitch.

claims.spoken: Dealership staff got incentive payments tied to enrollment.
requires: Alleged.

claims.spoken: G M ended Smart Driver in April twenty twenty-four.
requires: Per the complaint.

claims.spoken: Now G M needs a driver's clear yes before it collects or shares driving data.
requires: Per the settlement. Affirmative express consent.

claims.spoken: G M must limit what it collects to what is reasonably necessary.
requires: Per the settlement.

claims.spoken: Dealers must be trained so customers accept the privacy terms themselves.
requires: Per the settlement; within sixty days of the effective date.

claims.spoken: G M must delete driving data it kept from before January sixteenth, twenty twenty-five, with exceptions.
requires: Per the settlement. Exceptions include litigation holds and safety or recall uses.

claims.spoken: G M admitted no violation of law.
requires: Per the settlement.

claims.spoken: The settlement sets up no claims process for individual drivers.
requires: Absence checked in decree para 72; consumers get deletion and copy requests instead.

claims.spoken: Drivers can ask G M for a copy of their data or ask it to delete it.
claims.on_screen: ASK FOR A COPY · ASK FOR DELETION
requires: Per decree paras 61, 64.

claims.spoken: The acting attorney general said it reinforces the commitment to safeguarding Alaskans' personal information.
requires: Quote only: 'This holds GM accountable and reinforces our commitment to safeguarding Alaskans' personal information.' Cori Mills.

claims.spoken: The number of Alaska drivers affected isn't stated anywhere.
requires: Absence checked in the news stories, WA release and decree.
